audience: First-year physics students; no particle physics needed.
name: Going underground for dark matter
notes: Working title. Depths are rock thickness as each laboratory or experiment states it (SNOLAB: the 2 km quoted for DEAP-3600); m.w.e. also depends on the rock, which question 3 shows.

steps.text: The Cryogenic Dark Matter Search (CDMS II) experiment was located at the Soudan Underground Laboratory, which lies 705 m underground (2070 meters-water-equivalent). It used 19 germanium and 11 silicon particle detectors, operated below 50 mK.
steps.title: Soudan: 705 m down

steps.text: The 1400 metre-rock thickness above the Gran Sasso Laboratory provides a cosmic ray flux reduction by one million times. XENON1T, in Hall B there, held 3.2 tonnes of liquid xenon, 2.0 tonnes of it the active target, and ran from 2015 until 2018.
steps.title: Gran Sasso: a million times fewer cosmic rays

DEAP-3600 sits 2 km underground (6000 meters water equivalent overburden)
can hold 3600 kg of liquid argon

question.answer: The inner radius is 85 cm = 0.85 m, so the volume is 4/3 × π × (0.85 m)³ ≈ 2.57 m³. Dividing, 3600 kg ÷ 2.57 m³ ≈ 1400 kg/m³.

claims.covers: an inner radius of 85 cm and can contain 3600 kg of liquid argon

question.prompt: DEAP-3600's spherical acrylic vessel has an inner radius of 85 cm and can contain 3600 kg of liquid argon. What density of liquid argon does that imply?

steps.text: SNOLAB is a deep underground laboratory which uses the 2 km of rock overburden to filter out cosmic-ray muons. DEAP-3600 sits 2 km underground (6000 meters water equivalent overburden) and can hold 3600 kg of liquid argon.
steps.title: SNOLAB: 2 km of rock

claims.covers: LZ is located at the 4850-foot level of the Sanford Underground Research Facility in Lead, South Dakota
monitors 7 active tonnes of liquid xenon
released on 7 July 2022
were consistent with a background-only hypothesis
rejected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at a WIMP mass of 36 GeV/c² at the 90% confidence level

question.answer: LUX: 85.3 days × 118 kg ≈ 10,100 kg·days. LZ: 1000 days × 5500 kg = 5,500,000 kg·days. The ratio is 5,500,000 ÷ 10,100 ≈ 550, so about 550 times larger.

claims.covers: 85.3 live days with a 118 kg fiducial volume
its planned 1000 live days
a 5.5 t fiducial mass

question.prompt: LUX's first result used 85.3 live days with a 118 kg fiducial volume. Suppose LZ runs its planned 1000 live days with a 5.5 t fiducial mass. How many times larger is LZ's exposure (mass × live days)?

steps.text: LZ is located at the 4850-foot level of the Sanford Underground Research Facility in Lead, South Dakota (4300 m.w.e.), and monitors 7 active tonnes of liquid xenon. Its first results, released on 7 July 2022, were consistent with a background-only hypothesis and rejected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at a WIMP mass of 36 GeV/c² at the 90% confidence level.
steps.title: SURF: the LZ experiment

steps.text: PandaX-4T was located 2400 m underground at the Jinping site in Sichuan. It was commissioned in 2021 and started data taking then, with a design of 6 tonnes of xenon in total and a 4 tonne sensitive target.
steps.title: Jinping: 2400 m of rock

question.answer: Soudan: 2070 ÷ 705 ≈ 2.9. SURF: 4300 ÷ 1478 ≈ 2.9. SNOLAB: 6000 ÷ 2039 ≈ 2.9. At all three sites each metre of depth counts for about 2.9 m.w.e.

question.prompt: Soudan is 705 m underground, at 2070 m.w.e.; SURF is 1478 m down, at 4300 m.w.e.; the SNO detector vessel at SNOLAB is 2039 m below the surface, at about 6000 m.w.e. For each, divide the m.w.e. figure by the depth in metres. What do you notice?

steps.text: Soudan lies 705 m underground, Gran Sasso has a 1400 metre-rock thickness above it, SURF is 1478 m down, SNOLAB has 2 km of rock overburden and Jinping 2400 m.
steps.title: Five laboratories, five depths

summary: Visit five underground laboratories, from Soudan in Minnesota to Jinping in Sichuan, to see why dark matter searches go deep and what they found.
